title: Safe buyers, a clean first shipment and your 90-day plan
course_title: Export Readiness (Selected Products): From Local Seller to First Export Shipment

say: Safe buyers, a clean first shipment, and your 90-day plan.
This is the video for Module 3 of Export Readiness.
A buyer is not real until you have checked who they are and agreed how you will be paid. New exporters lose more money to poor payment terms and fake buyers than to shipping accidents.

panel.heading: What this module covers
items: Find and check real buyers
Choose safe payment terms
Run the first shipment without mistakes
Plan the next 90 days

say: Then you run a first shipment where every document agrees, and turn your remaining gaps into a dated plan.

say: Meet buyers through NEPC, diaspora shops, trade fairs, or larger exporters who need more supply. Then check them. Get the full company details, and check the register. For UK companies, Companies House is free online.

panel.heading: Five checks before you trust anyone
items: Full company name, number, address, website
Check the company register in their country
Look at the email domain
Video call with practical questions
Ask for a trade reference

say: A real importer rarely uses only a free email address for big orders. Hold a video call and ask which products they import and which documents their customs need. Ask for a trade reference.

panel.heading: Five checks before you trust anyone
items: Full company name, number, address, website
Check the company register in their country
Look at the email domain
Video call with practical questions
Ask for a trade reference

say: For example, Chioma in Aba gets a WhatsApp message. A man says he represents a major Canadian importer, wants 5 tonnes of dried hibiscus monthly, and asks for 10 kg of free samples and a supplier registration fee.

panel.heading: Chioma gets a suspicious enquiry
left: Fee to be paid to his agent
right: Asks for company details, video call
200 g sample, courier paid by buyer

say: She replies politely. She asks for company details and a video call, and offers a 200 g sample with the courier paid by the buyer. She does not pay fees, and first orders need a 50% deposit. The buyer stops replying. Chioma lost nothing.

say: Cash in advance is safest for you. A letter of credit means the buyer's bank pays if your documents match exactly, so a small spelling error can delay payment.

panel.heading: From safest to riskiest for you
items: Cash in advance, or a deposit: safest
Letter of credit: documents must match
Documentary collection: medium risk
Open account: only for trusted buyers

say: With documentary collection, the buyer can refuse the documents and leave goods at the port. Open account means you ship first and wait. Keep that for buyers you know and trust.

panel.heading: From safest to riskiest for you
items: Cash in advance, or a deposit: safest
Letter of credit: documents must match
Documentary collection: medium risk
Open account: only for trusted buyers

say: Never share your bank PIN, passwords or one-time codes with anyone. Fraudsters send fake new bank details, so confirm any change by phone on a number you already know.

say: Airlines charge the higher of actual weight and volumetric weight. Ngozi's forwarder uses a factor of 6,000. Her ginger cartons are heavy, so they are charged at their actual weight. But her light scarf carton is big, so it counts as 16 kg.

panel.heading: Ngozi checks her chargeable weight
items: 6 ginger cartons: charged at actual 84 kg
Scarf carton: 6 kg, but 16 kg by volume
Total charged: 100 kg, not 90 kg
Smaller scarf box: 6 kg by volume
Saves 10 kg of freight

say: So she pays for 100 kg, though the goods weigh 90. She folds the scarves tightly into a smaller box, and saves 10 kg of freight with no change to the goods.

panel.heading: Ngozi checks her chargeable weight
items: 6 ginger cartons: charged at actual 84 kg
Scarf carton: 6 kg, but 16 kg by volume
Total charged: 100 kg, not 90 kg
Smaller scarf box: 6 kg by volume
Saves 10 kg of freight
panel.rule: You pay for the higher of actual and volumetric weight.

say: Most first-shipment problems are small mismatches. Copy names and descriptions from one master sheet into the commercial invoice, packing list and certificates.
Give each helper a role, and have a second person check every line separately. A shortcut a local customer forgives can get goods refused at a foreign port.

panel.heading: Pre-shipment document check
items: Names and addresses match everywhere
Weights match packing list and cartons
Incoterm and place on the invoice
Certificates attached and in date
Copies sent to the buyer

say: Turn every gap into an action with an owner, a target week and a cost from a real quote. Days 1 to 30 are registrations and questions. Days 31 to 60, product work. Days 61 to 90, a paid sample, a quote and a shipment file.
In week 1 Amina registers with NEPC, and in week 2 she asks the buyer and NAQS which documents Ghana needs.

card.title: Amina's 90-day budget
card.note: Example estimates from quotes, plus NEPC fees.

say: She budgets about 150,000 naira for lab testing if the buyer requires it, 85,000 for labels and cartons, with her sister Hadiza as packing lead, and 20,000 for the shipment file.

card.title: Amina's 90-day budget
card.note: Example estimates from quotes, plus NEPC fees.

say: That is about 255,000 naira plus NEPC fees. Every Friday she ticks off what is done. If your product needs volume, consider group supply under a written agreement.

card.title: Amina's 90-day budget

say: To remember. Check every buyer, and start with cash in advance or a deposit. Protect your bank codes. Make every document agree, with a second checker.
And after each shipment, ask the buyer for feedback and fix issues before you grow.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check every buyer before you trust them
Start with a deposit or cash in advance
Never share PINs or one-time codes
Every document must agree
Gaps become dated, costed actions

say: Now write your buyer-check message and payment terms, prepare a practice shipment file, and write your 90-day plan with a budget.
